notes: Whether the ellipsis counts toward the n-character budget (candidate 1 appends beyond n; the rest keep the result within n).
Three ASCII dots '...' vs the single Unicode character U+2026 (affects both output and how much text survives).
When n is smaller than the ellipsis: return the bare prefix, a partial ellipsis, the full ellipsis anyway, or raise.
Negative n: raise ValueError vs clamp to 0 vs Django-style 'always emit ellipsis'.
n == 0 on a non-empty string: '' vs '...' vs U+2026.
Counting code points vs user-perceived characters (combining marks free, NFC normalization), and whether normalization leaks into the returned string.
Whether to back up to a word boundary rather than cutting mid-word.
Whether trailing whitespace just before the ellipsis is stripped.

Fixed by constraints: ellipsis is the single char '…' and counts toward n; n==0 -> ''; n<0 -> ValueError; 'characters' are code points of the NFD-decomposed string (so 'é' costs 2 and its accent is dropped at the cut) — all candidates honor this.
n == 1 on a longer string: return just '…' (candidates 1,2,4,5,6) vs keep the first character with no ellipsis because an ellipsis alone conveys nothing (candidate 3).
Whitespace immediately before the cut: kept ('hello …', candidates 1,3,5) vs stripped ('hello…', candidates 2,4,6).
Cut mid-word (most candidates) vs back up to the last word boundary when the cut lands inside a word (candidate 4).
Cut that removes only trailing whitespace: still ellipsized ('hell…') vs returned trimmed with no ellipsis ('hello') (candidate 6).
Trailing punctuation before the ellipsis: kept ('hello,…') vs stripped ('hello…') (candidate 6).
Accents/ligatures: only lost when they fall at the cut (candidates 1-4,6) vs folded away everywhere, even when nothing is truncated ('naïve café' -> 'naive cafe', 'ﬁsh' -> 'fish') (candidate 5).
